chats.answer:
A solar generator can run a well pump, but you need one powerful enough to handle the pump's startup surge, not just its normal running wattage.

For most residential wells, I would look for a solar generator with 240V output, at least 3,000–5,000W continuous power, and high surge capacity.

The right size depends mainly on your well pump's horsepower (HP) and whether it runs on 120V or 240V.

Neither is guaranteed to start every well pump. A motor's locked-rotor amperage is particularly important. Also, solar panels are generally purchased separately, and a hardwired pump needs a properly installed transfer switch or equivalent safe connection.
